feature: Order list: search, filters, saved views, bulk

shopify.text: Native. The Orders page has keyword search and filters, six default views (All, Unfulfilled, Unpaid, Open, Archived, Local Delivery) plus custom saved views (filters, columns, sort; saved on desktop only), and bulk actions on selected orders: fulfil, print packing slips, capture payment, archive, cancel (up to 250 at once), tags, labels, run a Flow workflow.

gap: Built and held by tests (wave 3 run 2, D173, in production since 6 October 2026). The Orders page reads its whole state from the address (`parseOrderListParams()`, the one parser) and builds every condition in `orderListWhere()`: search over number, email, name, line title, SKU, tag and tracking number (words escaped and bound, AND over at most five words, an erased person not found by email or name, no other store's order); filters for status, payment, fulfilment, tag, market, source, gift, archive and a store-day date range; keyset paging 50 at a time (250 orders walked with each of the four sorts, none lost or repeated; the total sort compares converted totals in a store with several currencies, a review fix); named views per store, 30 at most, opening one gives the orders its parameters typed give; and bulk tag, untag, archive, unarchive and mark as sent on up to 250 ticked orders or on 'all matching' (the query is re-read on the server), each order in its own transaction with every refusal named, one audit entry a batch, plus bulk packing slips without prices. The four criteria hold at the server and action layer (order-list, order-views, order-bulk and order-actions integration tests, run 2026-10-06 on a fresh database: 14 integration files, 286 tests, and the 6 of the action file, all passed). Held at Partial because the feature is the screen and no test clicks it: there is no signed-in admin browser fixture, so the filter bar, the selection state, the 'all matching' confirmation, the view bar and the cursor links are held by `renderToString` view tests only, and `page.tsx`'s own glue is type-checked, not run; the spec's forced-failure test of per-order atomicity (a failure on the third order leaves the first two applied) was not written, the property is read in `runBulk()` and held by the refusal tests; the 5,000-order timing test uses a generous bound on a test database and the spec calls it flaky on a busy one, so there is no measure on a real store's data. Not built, deliberately (spec section 7): bulk cancel, refund and capture, labels, Flow, a Local Delivery view, saved views per person, exporting the filtered list. Full after the signed-in by-hand pass of spec 9.7 item 1 is done and accepted.
criteria: Searching an order number, customer name, email or product title finds the matching orders of this store and no other store's (integration test).
The list filters by status, payment, fulfilment and a date range, all in the address, and pages through more than 200 orders without losing any (integration test with 250 orders).
A staff member saves a filter and column choice as a named view and reopens it (integration test; views are per store).

Selecting several orders offers bulk actions: add and remove tags, archive and mark sent, each applied to every selected order or reporting which one it refused; packing slips are printed for every selected order that has something to ship, the others listed with the reason (integration test).

shopify.text: Native. The order details page has a timeline of events and staff comments that are internal and never shown to the customer; payment and fulfilment statuses are tracked per order.

criteria: Every order event (placed, paid, sent, refunded, restocked, cancelled, edited, note, return steps) is stored append-only and cannot be edited or deleted (database test).
The order page lists the events and every email the customer got in one history, newest first, with return steps in plain words and a link to the return.
A staff note is added to the history, is visible only to staff, and is refused on copied history.
The order's status label follows its payment and shipments, and an order cancelled after payment stays listed as cancelled and refunded.

shopify.text: Native. Order tags (up to 250 per order, 40 characters each) can be added one by one or in bulk; most finished orders are archived automatically and can be archived or unarchived by hand; both are bulk actions and filters.

criteria: Staff add and remove tags on an order and on a selection of orders; tags are per store, case-insensitive, at most 40 characters, at most 250 per order (unit and integration tests).
The order list filters by tag and the tag shows on the order page and in its history (integration test).

Staff archive and unarchive orders singly and in bulk; archived orders leave the default list, stay reachable in an Archived view and keep their numbers and sequence (integration test, `order_number_audit` unchanged).
A copied order (D129) can be tagged and archived but nothing else about it changes.

history.why: Wave 3 run 2 (docs/wave-3-orders.md, D173 proposed; working tree not committed, migrations not applied to production). Read order-tags.ts, order-archive.ts, the two migrations' rules (tag limit trigger, `orders_archived_not_pending`, the two patched copied-order guards), ops-actions.ts and the order page's Tags card and Archive button, and ran on a fresh database: order-tags.test.ts, order-archive.test.ts, orders-ops.test.ts (PGlite, every migration), order-page-views.test.ts, order-tags.int.test.ts, order-archive.int.test.ts, order-bulk.int.test.ts and order-actions.int.test.ts (added in this step: the actions behind the tag card and the archive button, permission asked, text typed, refusal words, another store's order, copied history), all passed. Criterion 1: 40 code points, 250 an order (trigger, two concurrent writers), case-insensitive key, per store, singly and in bulk. Criterion 2: the tag filter, the tag on the order page and the `order.tags_changed` event with the words in `data.note`. Criterion 3: archive and unarchive singly, in bulk and automatically (off by default), out of the default list and in the Archived view, `order_number_audit()` and every number identical before and after, a return unarchives. Criterion 4: a copied order takes tags and archive and every other write still raises. Caveat: no test clicks the signed-in admin; the tag card, the archive button and the bulk bar are held by view tests and by the action tests, and a by-hand pass (spec 9.7 item 1) is still advised.

shopify.text: Native. After purchase staff can add or remove products, change quantities, change shipping fees, apply or remove manual discounts and edit customer details; extra payment is collected with an updated invoice and a lower total is refunded.

gap: Built and held by tests (D174, docs/wave-3-fulfilment.md): staff add, remove and lower lines of a paid order with nothing sent at `/admin/{store}/orders/{orderId}/edit` (`previewOrderEdit()`/`applyOrderEdit()`/`sendOrderEdit()` in `src/server/order-edits.ts`, priced by `priceOrderEdit()` in `src/lib/order-edit.ts`); kept units keep their sold price and discounts, added goods equal `cartSummary()` in a krone market and a euro view; a lower total is refunded through `refundOrder()` under the order lock before Stripe is asked (`refundChange()`), split over the order's payments (`splitRefund()`); a higher total is applied only when the customer pays the link (`/s/{store}/{market}/account/change/{token}`, `src/server/order-edit-pay.ts`) or staff record it as paid outside Kaizen (cash ceiling included); one `order.edit_applied` event, the number unchanged; a credit note and an additional invoice referring to the original. Verified on 2026-10-07 on a fresh database: the cited unit, PGlite, view and integration tests pass (118 integration tests in 12 files, 317 unit tests in 17 files). Still short of Full: (1) the consumer texts of docs/wave-3-fulfilment.md section 8 (the change emails, the change pay page, the edit invoice and credit note words, the cash-ceiling question 8) are hand-written and not yet read by a person; (2) no change has been paid in Stripe test mode on a real store (spec 9.7): the pay link is held only by the repo's fake Stripe; (3) e2e/order-change.spec.ts fails at line 37 (run on 2026-10-07 against a fresh build: 14 of 15 pass): it still expects the withdrawal sentence the review fix reworded ("Du kan angre kjøpet av varene som er lagt til innen 14 dager"), so the pay page's main e2e test is red until the spec is updated; (4) a refund owed after a change's pending refund fails shows on the order page and in the store checkup but not in the control center; a lower-total change holds the order's row lock while Stripe answers, and a database failure after Stripe's answer leaves that refund for the webhook to record; no test covers a D153 return refund after a paid change, and `tax-reports.int.test.ts` has no edit made in a later quarter (the reconciliation case is in `analytics-edits.int.test.ts`). Merged here on 2026-10-07: `checkout.order-editing-after-purchase` (the same Shopify feature and page, README rule 8); its criteria are criteria 3 to 5 below.
criteria: Staff add a line, remove a line and lower a quantity on a paid, unsent order; units kept keep the price and discounts they were sold with, added goods are priced and taxed by the checkout's own functions and agree with `cartSummary()` for the same goods, and the totals, VAT and stock follow (integration test in two currencies).

A higher total sends the customer a pay link for the difference and the change is applied when it is paid; a lower total refunds the difference through `refundOrder()` in the same transaction as the change and returns the stock (integration test with faked Stripe).
Every edit is one event in the order history with before and after, logged with who and when, and the order number and sequence do not change (D141).
An order with anything sent (partly sent included), a cancelled, a copied or a host order refuses line edits with a plain message.
The customer is emailed a revised confirmation when an edit is applied.

feature: Cancel order with refund and restock

shopify.text: Native. A paid, unfulfilled order can be cancelled with a refund to the original method, as store credit or later; items are restocked by default and the customer is notified by default; a partially fulfilled order cannot be cancelled; bulk cancel is limited to 250 orders.

gap: Evidence debt: no test covers cancelling an unpaid weekly delivery without a refund (`cancelOrder()`, `src/server/order-admin.ts`) or the download links ending; the core path (refund, restock, close, refuse after sent) is tested in `order-admin.int.test.ts`. The cancel event stores the reason, not the account. Shopify also cancels with a refund as store credit; Kaizen has none, counted once in checkout.refunds-and-cancellation.
criteria: Cancelling a paid, unsent order refunds everything left through Stripe on the store's account, puts every physical unit back in stock, closes the order and stops its download links (integration test).
An order that is already sent cannot be cancelled and the message says to refund instead (integration test).
An unpaid weekly delivery is cancelled without a refund and its stock is released.
The history says that staff cancelled and why; the customer is emailed when the box is ticked (ticked by default).

feature: Partial and full refunds with restocking

shopify.text: Native. Full or partial refunds per line item with quantities, optional restocking (on by default when inventory is tracked), refundable shipping, status Partially refunded; no stated time limit.

criteria: A refund of any amount up to what is left goes through Stripe on the store's account with Kaizen's fee on the refunded part returned, and more than is left is refused (integration test).
Staff choose which units go back in stock, with or without money back, never more than were bought or already restocked (integration test).

A return's refund is worked out once by `refundFor()` from what was paid after every discount, the delivery only for a whole-order withdrawal and minus return shipping the shopper pays, and is claimed before Stripe is called so two staff cannot pay it twice (unit and integration tests).
An order paid outside Kaizen's Stripe records the refund as made outside and still restocks (integration test).

shopify.text: Native. Draft orders let staff create orders for phone, in-person or email sales, with custom pricing, and send an invoice with a secure checkout link, take a card manually or mark the order paid; drafts created from 1 April 2025 are deleted after a year of inactivity.

gap: Built and held by tests (wave 3 run 2, D173, in production since 6 October 2026): staff make a draft (`D-n`, its own counter) with goods, custom service items, a custom price, a staff discount, shipping (rate, free or set) and a market, priced only by `priceDraft()` (equal to `cartSummary()` for the same goods in kroner and in a euro view, `checkout-kinds` draft scenarios); Send makes the order from the one shared insert `order-insert.ts` (next number of D141's sequence, stock held to the draft's expiry), emails a pay link (hashed token, `/account/pay/{token}`, Stripe's hosted page) and `applySession()` completes it; staff can instead record money taken outside Kaizen (a `manual` payment with a method, a received day, owner-only unless the owner allows staff, cash ceilings as data), which the invoice states as paid outside and whose refund is recorded with no Stripe call, capped under the order lock and by a trigger, and gets a credit note; an expired draft cancels its order, releases the stock and leaves the numbers whole; a staff-made order counts in sales, VAT and customers and not in conversion, the funnel or channels. The 16 findings of the review are fixed, each with a test (`draft-security.review.int.test.ts`, 7 tests). Run on a fresh database 2026-10-06: the integration files named in the evidence, the PGlite and unit files and `e2e/draft-pay.spec.ts` on a fresh production build (8 passed) all passed. Held at Partial for these reasons. (1) Consumer legal text nobody has read (spec section 8 items 1 to 3, 5, 6, 10 to 12): the pay page's states and right-of-withdrawal sentence, the 'Pay now' button against CRD Art. 8(2), the pay-link email and the store's quoted note, the invoice and credit-note wording for a payment taken outside Kaizen, the cash warnings, the staff-discount line, the retention of a draft's contact data, and the received-day rule that decides the VAT and OSS period; and the cash ceilings in `cash-limits.ts` are `verified: false` (Norway's 40,000 NOK is enforced, Denmark's warns, no other country is held, which is not a statement that there is no rule). A person must read them. (2) The Stripe link flow has run only against the repo's fake Stripe (a hosted session, the webhook path through `applySession()`, the refund); no real test-mode session, webhook or refund has run, and the e2e cannot follow the button to Stripe (spec 9.7 item 2). (3) No test clicks the signed-in admin: the draft editor, send dialog and paid-outside dialog are held by `renderToString` view tests, and the draft actions (`saveDraftAction`, `sendDraftAction`, `recordPaidOutsideAction` and the rest) are not exercised directly. (4) The criterion that a draft-created order is in the customer's history rests on `linkOrderToCustomer()` and `listCustomerOrders()` reading `customer_id`, and no test asserts that a paid draft order appears there (the analytics test counts the customer, the privacy test exports drafts). (5) Product limits that are decisions, not bugs: a custom service item is sold to businesses only (`custom_consumer`) because the withdrawal function answers any service as a booking; a delivery address must be in the market's country (a blocking problem; the field is not locked); `payments.received_on` dates the invoice and the VAT and OSS reports but the `order.paid` event and analytics still date the sale by the day it was recorded, so Finance and the VAT report can place a late-recorded payment in different periods. Not built, deliberately (spec section 7): subscriptions, appointments, stays, downloads and hosts' listings on a draft, codes, campaigns, credits and VAT-number checks, carrier quotes, deposits and payment terms, card details by phone, a reminder before the link expires.
criteria: Staff create a draft with products, quantities, a customer, address, shipping and a discount; totals and VAT come from the checkout's own functions (integration test in two currencies).

Sending the draft emails a pay link; the order is made when it is sent, paying it completes it, the number is from the store's gap-free sequence (D141), and stock is held only from the send (integration test).

A draft can be marked paid for money taken outside Kaizen (cash, bank transfer) with the method recorded; a refund of such an order is recorded with no Stripe call, a credit note follows from the existing trigger, and the amount is capped at what is left.
An unpaid draft that expires cancels its order, leaves the number sequence without a gap (`order_number_audit` clean) and releases its stock.
Draft-created orders count in sales and in the customer's history and are marked as staff-made.

history.why: Wave 3 run 2 (docs/wave-3-orders.md, D173 proposed; working tree not committed). Read draft-orders.ts, draft-pay.ts, draft-sessions.ts, order-insert.ts, payment-session.ts, order-admin.ts's manual refund branch, the pay page and the migrations, and ran on a fresh database: the draft, order-list, payment-reader and cash-limit unit files, orders-ops.test.ts and invoice-parity.test.ts (PGlite), draft-orders.int.test.ts, draft-security.review.int.test.ts, checkout-kinds.int.test.ts (draft scenarios in krone and euro), analytics-staff-orders.int.test.ts, the view tests, and e2e/draft-pay.spec.ts on a fresh production build; all passed. Every criterion is built and held by tests, but the row rests on consumer legal text no person has read (spec section 8), on cash ceilings marked unverified, on a Stripe flow run only against the fake Stripe, and on admin screens no test clicks; the customer-history half of criterion 5 has no test of its own. Bucket D as for D172's unreviewed delivery wording: the review is people's work. Re-bucket to A when a person has read the texts.

shopify.text: Native. Orders are fulfilled singly, in bulk or in batches that pick, pack and print; an order can be partly fulfilled by entering item quantities, each fulfilment with its own tracking number and notification, and the order status page shows a section per fulfilment.

gap: Built and held by tests (wave 3 run 3, docs/wave-3-fulfilment.md, D174): parcels name their lines and units (`shipment_lines`, `markSent()`), an order stays paid and Partly sent while units are left, each parcel has its own carrier, tracking and email listing its lines, the shopper's order pages list the parcels, bulk Mark as sent sends the remainder and names each refusal, and withdrawn units are never sent. Units refunded before they were sent leave what is to send when staff tick *These units were not sent* (`commerce.unsent_closures`, `refundOrder({ notSent })`, `src/server/unsent-closures.int.test.ts` in kroner and euros: an order of 3 with 1 sent and 2 closed becomes Sent, its slip, the pick list and bulk send leave them out, and a closed unit is never offered for withdrawal); criterion 5 is held. Still short of Full: (1) Spec 6.2 F2 names "carrier bookings pass their lines (fake carrier)": `bring-shipping.int.test.ts`, `helthjem-shipping.int.test.ts` and `porterbuddy-shipping.int.test.ts` never book a part of an order, so a carrier-booked partial parcel is held by no test; Bring also refuses a second booking of the same order within two minutes, so two Bring parcels of one order cannot be booked back to back. (2) The staff Send card is held by view tests, the form parser and `markSent()` integration tests only (no signed-in admin e2e, D158); spec 9.7's by-hand check is not done. (3) The receipt sentence and the parcel words shown to consumers (spec section 8 items 6 and 7) are not yet read by a person.
criteria: Staff mark chosen lines and quantities as sent in one shipment; the order shows Partly sent until every physical unit not withdrawn is in a shipment and Sent after (integration test).
Each shipment has its own carrier, tracking and email; the shopper's order page lists them with their lines.
Selecting several orders marks them sent in one action, reporting any that were refused (integration test).
Units withdrawn before sending (D153) are left out of what can be fulfilled.

Units refunded or taken off before they were sent are no longer to send: the order's packing slip, the pick list and the bulk send leave them out, and an order whose remaining units were all refunded shows Sent, without a parcel of refunded goods (integration test).

history.why: Wave 3 run 3 (docs/wave-3-fulfilment.md, D174 proposed): shipments name their lines and units (`shipment_lines`, `markSent()` with `lines`, everything still to send without them), an order stays paid and Partly sent until no unit not withdrawn is left to send (`toSend()` = `commerce.line_to_send()`, withdrawals only after the review fix), each parcel has its own carrier, tracking and email listing its lines, the shopper's order pages list parcels and what is still to come, bulk Mark as sent sends a partly sent order's remainder and names each refusal, and withdrawn units are left out of sends, slips and the pick list. Read in the code and re-run on 2026-10-07 on a fresh database: src/server/fulfilment.int.test.ts, order-bulk.int.test.ts, returns.int.test.ts and order-edit-review-fixes.int.test.ts, the PGlite src/db/fulfilment.test.ts, the unit and view tests, and e2e/partial-shipment.spec.ts (5 of 5 against a fresh build). The staff Send card is held by view tests, the form parser by unit tests and markSent() by integration tests; no signed-in admin e2e exists (D158), so the by-hand check of spec 9.7 is the lead's before the push.

Skeptic of the wave 3 run 3 re-rate. I re-ran the cited tests on my own database w3_wave_3_fulfilment_skeptic: fulfilment, order-bulk, packing-slips, pick-list, returns and order-edit-review-fixes integration tests (72 of 72), and the unit and view tests (146 passed, 1 skipped). All pass, but they never refund an unsent unit. A throwaway integration test (deleted afterwards) did what the cancel refusal tells staff to do on a partly sent order: an order of 3, 1 sent, the 2 unsent refunded through `refundOrder()` with restock. The order stayed paid and Partly sent with 2 to send. The slip and pick list printed the 2 refunded units, and bulk Mark as sent recorded a second parcel of them, after which the order was Sent with the units both restocked and shipped. I read `commerce.line_to_send()` (quantity − shipped − withdrawn) in supabase/migrations/20261006235336_fulfilment_rules.sql and `cancelOrder()`/`editBlock()`: a partly sent order has no other way to drop its remainder. So criterion 1's 'Sent after' cannot be reached honestly and criterion 3's bulk send ships refunded goods. This is the same class of defect as the fixed review finding about returns stranding a partly sent order. Also missing: spec 6.2 F2's carrier-booking parcel test (none of the three carrier integration tests books part of an order).

feature: Flat shipping rate with free threshold

shopify.text: Native. Flat rates, order-amount and weight-based rates, free shipping, per zone and per profile, set under Settings > Shipping and delivery.

criteria: Each market has one flat shipping price, VAT-inclusive, with an optional basket value over which shipping is free; the charge is the flat price below the threshold and zero at or over it (unit test).
The cart, checkout and the placed order charge the same shipping, in the shopper's currency, and a market with no price refuses checkout with a message (integration test).
The owner edits the rates per market on the shipping settings page.
The flat rate stays as the default and the fallback when a carrier does not answer.

feature: Weight or price rate tables, zones, profiles

shopify.text: Native. Flat rates can carry conditions on order amount or on total weight (tiers), set per shipping zone (groups of countries or regions) and per shipping profile (rules for chosen products and locations); transit-time display and backup rates are native too.

gap: Flat rate per market with a free-above threshold, carrier-quoted weight pricing for connected carriers and a per-service weight limit; no merchant-defined weight or price tiers, no regions inside a country and no per-product shipping profiles. Rechecked at HEAD: unchanged.
criteria: An owner defines tiers by basket weight and by basket value per market; the charge is the tier that matches, and a basket in no tier is refused or falls to a stated default (unit test).
A zone groups postal-code ranges inside a country, with its own rates (unit test of matching, integration test of checkout).

A shipping profile assigns products to rates, and a mixed basket is charged by the stated rule (the dearest profile, or the sum), the same in `cartSummary()` and `placeOrder()` (integration test, euro scenario).
A product with no weight uses the store's default weight.

history.why: First report's skeptic recheck: carrier-quoted weight pricing and per-service weight limits exist for connected carriers, so not missing; no merchant-defined weight or price tiers, zones or profiles. Entry written in wave 0 from the first report, which did not log it.

shopify.text: Native, but conditional: third-party carrier-calculated shipping (UPS, FedEx, USPS, Canada Post, Australia Post) is included on Advanced and Plus; Grow adds it for an extra monthly fee or with annual billing. None of the Nordic carriers is among them.

gap: Live prices from Bring and Porterbuddy for Norway (D135, D137); PostNord and Helthjem services are priced by the store, not by the carrier; Sweden and Denmark have no live rates. Nothing has been checked against a real carrier's production service.
criteria: At checkout a Norwegian address gets the carrier's own price for each service, with VAT and the store's markup, shown in the shopper's currency (integration test with a faked carrier).
A carrier that does not answer within the timeout leaves the flat rate and the checkout works (integration test).
A carrier with a price service for Sweden and Denmark quotes there too, behind a sandbox check of the credentials.
`cartSummary()` and `placeOrder()` agree on the chosen service's price, in the euro view too.

shopify.text: Native in ten countries: labels are bought and printed in the admin with carriers in the US, Canada, Australia, the UK, France, Germany, Italy, the Netherlands, Poland and Spain; none in Norway, Sweden or Denmark. International labels need HS codes and a declared value under 2,500 USD; bulk label purchase exists.

gap: Booking with Bring (D134), Porterbuddy (D137) and Helthjem (D138), for parcels to Norway, with the label fetched from the carrier when printed and never stored; PostNord cannot book (D136, waiting for its EDI specification); in the store's test environment nothing real is booked; no bulk booking or printing; nothing verified against a carrier's live service.
criteria: From an order staff book a parcel with a connected carrier and the tracking number, consignment number and label address are kept on a shipment and the order is marked sent (integration tests with faked carriers).
The label is fetched from the carrier's own host with the store's key when printed and never kept (test).
Selecting several orders books and prints their labels in one action, reporting any that failed.
PostNord books once its specification is available, in its sandbox first.

feature: Pickup points and lockers at checkout

shopify.text: Native, for a few carriers and countries: pickup points (post offices, partner shops, lockers) are enabled per location in Settings > Shipping and delivery for Chronopost, Evri, Colissimo, Correos, Mondial Relay, Poste Italiane and Royal Mail (France, Italy, Spain, UK); on Plus a custom app can add others through the Pickup Point Delivery Option Generator API. Elsewhere, including the Nordics, merchants use carrier apps. First report had this as app-only.

gap: Pickup points for Bring (service 5800), PostNord and Helthjem collect (D135, D136, D138), chosen at checkout and kept on the order; Nordic only, nothing for DPD, InPost, Packeta or GLS. Criteria 1 and 2 are held by `delivery-options.int.test.ts`; criterion 3 is breadth beyond Shopify and needs no new agreement to be left out.
criteria: At checkout the shopper gives a postal code and picks one of the nearest points; the choice is kept on the order and shown in the admin, the order page and the emails (integration test).
A carrier that does not answer leaves the flat rate and no point is required.

Optional breadth beyond Shopify's own list (Chronopost, Evri, Colissimo, Correos, Mondial Relay, Poste Italiane, Royal Mail): a further carrier (DPD, InPost, Packeta or GLS) adds points through its adapter and the same piece, behind its own agreement and a sandbox test.

shopify.text: Native. Pickup in store is switched on per location; a Ready for pickup email goes to the customer when the order is marked ready, with the store's pickup instructions; available on standard plans.

gap: A store can list its shops and pickup places with address and opening hours (`store_locations`, kind `pickup`, D40), but they are information only: checkout offers no collect-from-store method, orders have no ready-for-pickup state and no email.
criteria: An owner switches pickup on for a store location with instructions and a price (free by default); checkout offers it as a delivery method for that market and `cartSummary()` and `placeOrder()` agree (integration test, euro scenario).
The order keeps the chosen location; staff mark it ready for pickup, which sends the customer an email in the order's language with the address, hours and instructions, once (integration test).
Marking it collected closes the order without a shipment, and the order is excluded from To send.

shopify.text: Native. Local delivery is set per location with a radius (up to 160 km) or a list of postal codes, up to 10 zones per location with up to 3 price rules each, a minimum order amount and a delivery price (0 for free).

gap: Porterbuddy's delivery windows for Norway (D137) and the subscription boxes' delivery rounds with a cutoff (D102); no merchant-defined delivery zones by radius or postal code, no minimum order amount, no own-driver route.
criteria: An owner defines a local delivery area by postal codes or a radius from a store location, with a price, a minimum basket and a free-above value; checkout offers it only inside the area (unit test of matching, integration test of checkout).
`cartSummary()` and `placeOrder()` agree on its price in the euro view too.
Orders for local delivery list apart for staff, with the address and any delivery note.

shopify.text: Native packing slips (single and bulk print from the Orders page) and pick lists, invoices and receipts through the free Order Printer app that Shopify builds and maintains; bulk printing up to 50 orders without opening the app; templates in HTML, CSS and Liquid.

criteria: Selecting several orders prints their packing slips in one document, one per page, in each order's language, without prices (integration test of the data, render test of the page).
A pick list adds up the items of the selected orders by product, variant, SKU and quantity, leaving out digital and service lines and units already sent or withdrawn before sending (unit test).
A slip shows a gift message when the order has one (with wave 3's gift rows).
Slips of orders of another store are never printed (integration test).

history.why: Re-read at HEAD: one printable packing slip per order, in the customer's language and without prices, and nothing else. Shopify prints packing slips in bulk (up to 50 orders) and has pick lists; with no bulk print and no pick list the row's own gap text contradicts Full (README rule 1: the criteria must hold). Not new code: the first report knew this and still rated it Full.

Wave 3 run 3 (docs/wave-3-fulfilment.md, D174 proposed) on top of D173's bulk slips: the bulk slips (`packingSlipData()`, at most 100 orders, one page each in the order's language, no prices) now print the units still to send and skip what has nothing left with a reason; a parcel's own slip (`parcelSlipData()`, `?shipment=`) says more follows and keeps the gift block; a pick list of the selected orders (`pickList()` in src/lib/pick-list.ts, `pickListData()`, `/admin/{store}/orders/pick-list`, a bulk action on the Orders list) sums by product, variant and SKU or lists by order, leaving out downloads, services and units sent or withdrawn; another store's ids are not found. Re-run on 2026-10-07 on a fresh database: packing-slips.int.test.ts, pick-list.int.test.ts and order-bulk.int.test.ts, and the unit and render tests pick-list.test.ts, packing-slip-views.test.ts and pick-list-view.test.ts. Template choice is not a criterion and is not built (spec section 7).

shopify.text: Native. A Shipping confirmation email goes with each fulfilment; each fulfilment has its own tracking number, link and notification; the template is editable in Settings > Notifications.

criteria: Marking an order sent emails the customer once, in the order's language, with the carrier, tracking number, a tracking button and the delivery address, and sending it again is refused as a duplicate unless staff ask for a resend (integration test).
The tracking link is the carrier's own page for Posten, Bring, PostNord, DHL and UPS, a pasted https link otherwise, and never a non-https address (unit test).
The email carries the right to withdraw and who pays return shipping as the order was sold (D153).

shopify.text: Native. Customers follow a parcel on the order status page (Confirmed, On its way, Out for delivery, Delivered, Attempted delivery) with a map for integrated carriers and a section per shipment; shipping update emails exist as templates; the Shop app also tracks.

gap: The shopper's order page shows each shipment's carrier and a tracking link; the carrier's latest event is shown to staff only (`carrierTracking()` for Bring, PostNord, Porterbuddy and Helthjem); no out-for-delivery or delivered email, no delivery timeline for the shopper, and a delivery is recorded only when staff press Mark received (D153, `delivered_at`).
criteria: The shopper's order page shows a parcel's events from the carrier (unit test of the mapping, integration test with a faked carrier) and says plainly when the carrier gives none.
A carrier's delivered event records `delivered_at` once, never earlier than the order and never over a staff date, and it starts the 14-day count of D153 (integration test).
Out-for-delivery and delivered emails go once per shipment, only when the store switched them on, in the order's language.
A carrier that does not answer leaves the tracking link and no error.

shopify.text: Native. Each customer notification template (order confirmation, shipping confirmation, shipping update, refund, ready for pickup and more) is editable under Settings > Notifications: subject and HTML body with Liquid variables, logo and brand colours, and each can be switched off.

gap: Wording and layout are fixed in code (`email-text.ts`, `email-layout.ts`; nb, sv, da, en by hand, other languages through the catalogue, D111); switches are per action, not per event; the store's logo and colours reach the layout but the owner cannot edit a subject or body. Rechecked at HEAD; D153 added its return emails to the same fixed set.
criteria: An owner edits the subject and a text block of an order email per language, with named placeholders only (no code), and a preview shows it with a sample order (unit and render tests).
Every order email can be switched off or on per event, and legally required ones (the withdrawal acknowledgement, the order confirmation) cannot be switched off.
An edited text passes the claims filter and the placeholder check before it is saved; a missing translation falls back to the fixed text.
Emails keep the order's language and currency, and edits are copied with a store only if the owner chooses.

history.why: First report's skeptic recheck: wording and layout are fixed in code and an owner cannot edit a subject or body; switches are per action, not per event. Entry written in wave 0 from the first report, which did not log it.

feature: Staff alerts for new orders, order automation

shopify.text: Native. Staff notifications (new order, store order summary daily or weekly, return requests, draft orders, disputes) go by email to the owner by default and to chosen staff or addresses, with push on the mobile app and an editable new-order template; Shopify Flow adds workflow automation.

gap: Order and customer events go to Slack, Zapier and Make (D41, D101); the store's contact address gets an email once per return whose refund is overdue (D153) and the store Home lists what needs attention; no new-order email or push to staff, no order summary, no rule builder.
criteria: Each paid order emails the staff the owner chose (default the owners) once, with the order number, total and a link; a retried webhook sends no second email (integration test).
Owners choose recipients and events (new order, return requested, refund overdue, low stock) and a daily or weekly summary (integration test).
A rule `when {event} and {condition} then {action}` (tag, notify, hold) is stored per store, runs once per event and is logged (unit test of matching, integration test).
Nothing in a staff email names a shopper's phone or full address.

shopify.text: Native. Self-serve returns let customers request a return or cancellation from their account or the order status page; the merchant reviews it from the Orders page (Customer request filter), approves or declines with a message, and can add exchange items, fees and a return label. No EU withdrawal button as such: Shopify's page describes returns, not the directive's two-step function.

criteria: A shopper withdraws in two steps (Withdraw from contract here, then Confirm withdrawal) with no reason asked; nothing is a withdrawal before the second press, and an unconfirmed request expires after 24 hours (integration test).
A wrong email, an unknown number and another store's order give the same answer after the same delay, and guesses are limited by hashed keys, never IP or cookie (integration test).

Confirming records the statement, creates the return, and emails the acknowledgement with date, time, lines and reference, kept in `email_messages`; a failing email leaves the withdrawal standing as not sent, resent by staff or the job (integration test).

Per line `lineEligibility()` says whether the right applies and why not (excluded goods, digital content with consent, business, booking, already returned); the 14 days count only from a recorded receipt (unit test).
The function sets no cookie or storage, is linked from the footer, the order page and the order emails, and a store's longer window offers a return request the store may decline (unit tests, e2e).

history.why: D153 shipped (commit 4ae6222, migrations applied to production and recorded in docs/decisions.md): the withdrawal function at /s/{store}/{market}/withdraw, return requests inside the store's own window, the status page, the acknowledgement on a durable medium; the tables the first report found unused are now read and written. Tests read: returns.int.test.ts, withdraw/actions.int.test.ts, withdrawal.test.ts, e2e/withdrawal.spec.ts.

shopify.text: Native. Merchants create returns from a fulfilled order or approve customer requests, with return rules (window, return shipping cost, restocking fee as a percentage); the financial outcome is worked out from fees and exchange items; return fees are not deducted from the refund automatically, staff do it by hand.

criteria: A return moves forward only (requested, approved, in transit, received, inspected, closed; declined and cancelled end it), enforced by the database and the pure table alike (database test over every move).

Inspection records per line a condition, restock yes or no and a deduction with a note never above the line's value; the refund is `refundFor()` of what was paid, minus deductions, minus return shipping the shopper pays (unit and integration tests).

A withdrawal return is never declined or cancelled and its refund cannot be lowered by staff; a voluntary return can be declined with a reason or refunded at a lower amount with a reason (integration tests).
The queue filters by status, kind and overdue, oldest first, and an overdue refund reaches the store Home and the control center (integration test).
Returns show in analytics (rate, reasons, products, time to refund) and the AI manager reads them; approve and decline are gated (tests).

history.why: D153 shipped the return object: `returns`/`return_lines`, numbers `{order}-R{n}`, lifecycle requested to closed enforced in SQL, reasons, inspection per line (condition, restock, deduction with note), return shipping, a refund worked out once and paid through `refundOrder()`, queue and detail screens, analytics. First report: refund-and-restock only. Read the code and tests at HEAD (returns.int.test.ts, returns-admin, returns-actions, src/db/returns.test.ts). Return labels and exchanges are separate rows and stay open.

shopify.text: Native, narrowly: return labels can be bought in the admin only for US domestic orders (USPS, FedEx, UPS); elsewhere merchants buy from a carrier or an app. When approving a self-serve return the merchant can create a label in Shopify, upload an existing label or choose no shipping; the label goes in the confirmation email.

gap: Staff paste a label address for a return (D153) and the shopper gets it; no return label is bought from a connected carrier, and none is created for the shopper to print on a self-serve request.
criteria: Approving a return with a connected carrier books a return shipment from the shopper's address to the return address and keeps its label address on the return (integration test with a faked carrier).
The label reaches the shopper by email and on the status page, fetched from the carrier's own host and never stored (test).
Who pays is the order's return cost payer: a label the shopper pays for is taken off the refund as return shipping (unit test with `refundFor()`).
A carrier that cannot book leaves the pasted-address path working.

history.why: D153 lets staff attach a return label address (https only, pasted) when approving or later; it is shown on the shopper's status page and emailed as a button, and tests hold it (returns.int.test.ts, returns-actions.int.test.ts, return-input.test.ts, return-status-view.test.ts). That matches Shopify's own 'upload an existing label' path, not its label purchase. Weak partial: Kaizen's carrier modules still book outbound only.

shopify.text: Native. Staff add exchange items to a return (not custom items; stock is not reserved until the return is processed); fees and exchange items are netted so the system shows a refund due or a payment to collect; the exchanged items have their own return window.

gap: Not built (D153 deliberately leaves exchanges out of `docs/returns.md`): a return refunds, nothing creates a replacement order or nets the difference.
criteria: Staff add replacement products to a return; the system shows the difference (refund due or payment to collect) from the same pricing functions as checkout, in two currencies (unit and integration tests).
Processing the return creates a linked new order for the replacements with a number from the store's sequence (D141), holding stock only then.
A difference owed by the shopper goes out as a pay link; one owed to the shopper is refunded through `refundOrder()` (integration test).
A withdrawal's legal refund is never reduced by choosing an exchange without the shopper's own statement.

shopify.text: App. Orders are fulfilled by the merchant, by a third-party fulfilment app or by Shopify Fulfillment Network, and the Help Center says only that merchants can use any of these; availability of the Network by country was not on the page read.

gap: Only outbound order events through Zapier, Make and Slack (D41, D101); a warehouse cannot send tracking or stock levels back, because there is no public API. Weak partial.
criteria: A warehouse provider with a scoped token reads paid orders to fulfil and posts a shipment with tracking, which marks lines sent and emails the customer (integration test; needs the Admin API of wave 9).
A provider posts stock levels per SKU, which update the inventory with an adjustment reason (integration test).
Events are signed and retried and a provider sees only its own store's data.

history.why: First report's skeptic recheck: outbound order events through Zapier, Make and Slack (D41, D101) make it a weak partial, not missing; a warehouse cannot send anything back without a public API. Entry written in wave 0 from the first report, which did not log it.

shopify.text: Native, conditional: duties and import taxes can be collected at checkout (DDP) when the store uses a carrier that supports DDP labels (Canada Post to the US, DHL Express, DHL eCommerce), products have HS codes and Shopify Fulfillment Network is not used; Managed Markets (Global-e as merchant of record, per-order fee) takes over customs entirely.

gap: No duty collection: HS code and country of origin are stored per variant (`product_variants.hs_code`, `origin_country`, edited in the product editor) but nothing uses them: no duty or import-VAT estimate at checkout, no customs data in carrier bookings, no IOSS. The fields are the prerequisite, not partial credit.
criteria: For a non-EU destination the checkout shows an estimated duty and import VAT from HS code, origin and value, worked out in code from a rates table the platform keeps, labelled as an estimate (unit and integration tests, euro scenario).
A booking to a non-EU country carries the customs lines (HS code, origin, value, description) and refuses to book without them (adapter test).
Whether duties are collected at checkout (DDP) or by the carrier (DAP) is the store's choice per market and is stated on the order and the emails.
IOSS registration is recorded per store and used only through an intermediary (bucket B part).

history.why: Skeptic recheck: HS code and origin are captured fields only; nothing computes, collects or transmits duties.

shopify.text: Native. Inventory is tracked per location, orders can be fulfilled from the location closest to the customer by routing rules based on availability and proximity, and locations also serve POS, pickup and fulfilment apps; the number of locations depends on the plan.

gap: Built and tested (wave 3, D172, in production since 6 October 2026): stock locations (add, rename, change country, rank by `priority`, owner-only deactivate and reactivate, never deleted, at least one active, at most 20); `allocate()` (`src/lib/stock-routing.ts`) names the rule once (keep an order together, else by rank, the backordered remainder at the first location that stocks the variant) and `placeOrder()` applies it with level rows locked in (variant, location) order, so two checkouts cannot deadlock (a race for the last unit is tested); `variant_availability` sells the sum of the active locations, each floored at zero; refund, cancel and return restock to the location the units came from or one staff choose (`restockPlan()`, `restockRoom()`), falling back to the first active location; `locationImpact()` reports units, variants and live holds before a deactivation, which is refused while checkouts hold stock there. Held by `stock-routing.test.ts`, `stock-routing.int.test.ts`, `inventory-locations.int.test.ts`, `stock-restock.test.ts`, `returns.int.test.ts`, the PGlite location guards and the view tests; every one passed in my runs. Why it stays Partial: (1) the locations page, the deactivate dialog and the refund dialog's 'Put back at' select have never been clicked (no signed-in admin fixture, D158): they are held by `renderToString` tests and by integration tests of the server functions; (2) criterion 4's guard is not reliable: `src/server/inventory-perf.int.test.ts` (the C4 guard) is not reliable: its 20-line `placeOrder()` timed out at 60 s in most of my runs against a database that already held an earlier perf store or ran other test files at the same time (probably stale planner statistics; the statement caught running for minutes was `orderLineRows()`'s cart-line read in `src/server/checkout.ts`, unchanged by this wave apart from two columns) and passed in 7 s alone on a fresh database, as in the Gates run; the cause is not found. (3) a hold's physical part is not re-checked against the shelf at payment, so staff who lower a level below live holds make those orders go negative with no backorder note (the Inventory page shows negative available; docs/wave-3-inventory.md 3.13); (4) with several active locations the product editor shows the total read-only and the bulk grid refuses a stock column, so stock per location is edited only on the Inventory page or by file; (5) one routing rule only: no closest-location or custom rules, no locations that do not fulfil online orders, no per-product or per-market locations, no transfers; a location's country is a label.
criteria: An owner adds, renames and deactivates stock locations; each variant's stock is held per location and the storefront sells the sum of the active ones (integration test).
An order's lines are assigned to locations by a stated rule (stock available, then priority) and holds are taken there under row locks (integration test).
A refund restocks to the location the line was taken from, or the one staff choose.
Stock reads and holds stay within a stated performance bound held by `inventory-perf.int.test.ts`.
Deactivating a location removes its stock from what is sellable and tells the owner how much was held there (units on hand and variants; it is refused while checkouts in progress hold stock there).

shopify.text: Native. Orders export to CSV from the Orders page (selected, current page or a date range; up to 50 orders download directly, larger exports are emailed), with customer, financial, fulfilment, line item, address, payment and tag columns, UTF-8.

criteria: The owner exports the orders of a date range or a list of order numbers as UTF-8 CSV with one row per line, in the order's own currency and the store's main currency, VAT split out (unit test of the columns, integration test of the rows).
A large export runs as a job and is delivered by a link to the signed-in owner, not emailed as an attachment (integration test).
Fields that start with = + - or @ are escaped against spreadsheet formulas, and copied history is marked as such (unit test).
An export contains only the signed-in member's store.

history.why: Wave 2, first run (docs/wave-2-data.md; working tree not yet committed). Read order-export.ts, order-csv.ts and the route and ran order-csv.test.ts, order-export.int.test.ts, checkout-kinds.int.test.ts, data-permissions.int.test.ts, data-jobs.int.test.ts, money-review.int.test.ts and privacy-erasure.int.test.ts (all passed). Criterion 1: one row per line with the contract's columns, the order's amounts on its first row only, order currency and main currency at the store's rate (blank and no_rate without one), the lines' VAT plus shipping VAT equal to the order's tax for every order, a range by the store's days including the 23 and 25 hour clock-change days of Europe/Oslo, a pasted list of order numbers with unknown ones listed back, and a euro scenario in checkout-kinds.int.test.ts that places an order in a euro view of a NOK store and holds the exported row. Criterion 2: above 2,000 rows a job in parts, the ready email carries no file and no link that works unsigned, the download is a 60 second signed address logged first (route handler called in the test). Criterion 3: formula characters escaped by the one writer (canary), copied orders left out unless asked and marked C-, host orders marked, an erased person's order has no personal field, Stripe test-mode orders are marked test_payment, no secret or token in any profile. Criterion 4: store isolation and a 404 for a member who is not the owner. Criteria reworded to what was built (docs/wave-2-data.md 6.6 points 2 and 4): the owner exports, and a selection is a list of order numbers plus an Export this order button (the order list with tick boxes is wave 3). Caveats: the file is the owner's data for an accountant, not a ledger; the VAT split columns and the personal-data defaults need an accountant's and a data-protection read (docs/wave-2-data.md section 8); the storage adapter has run only against a fake and the pages have no signed-in browser run (D158).

feature: Customer order status page and order history

shopify.text: Native. The order status page shows live shipping status and a section per shipment; customer accounts list the order history and let customers start returns where self-serve returns are on.

criteria: The order page shows lines, totals with VAT and every discount kind, payment state, delivery and pickup point, shipments with tracking links and bookings, in the order's language and currency (render tests).
The page is a page-builder role with pieces (D113, D117) and falls back to the standard page; it needs the order's own key or the signed-in customer and is not indexed.
A signed-in customer sees their orders in My account, each with the same detail page.
A paid order of goods offers the withdrawal and the order's returns with their status page (D153).

feature: Invoices and VAT receipts for orders

shopify.text: App: only through the free Order Printer app that Shopify builds (invoice, packing slip, pick list, receipt templates in HTML, CSS and Liquid, with invoice numbers, printed singly or up to 50 at a time); legal invoicing and credit notes are done by invoicing apps.

gap: Built and held by tests (unit 1b, D159, in production): `commerce.issue_order_invoice()` is called inside `complete_order_payment()` in a sub-block, so every paid path (checkout, renewal, standing delivery, venue booking) gets one invoice in the store's own gap-free series, frozen as a JSON snapshot, immutable (one-time `pdf_path` aside), with no delete and no direct insert; copied, host, Stripe-test-mode and invoicing-off orders get none, and a store with incomplete seller details, a non-registered seller whose order charged VAT or no exchange rate waits and is issued later; the shopper's order page and the hosted page `/account/documents/{token}` draw it from the snapshot, the PDF is the same view rendered by Chromium and stored once with the print page as fallback, the confirmation and shipped emails link it and attach the PDF when it exists, staff list, reprint, export and resend, and a reverse-charge or IOSS order says so with the numbers (checked through checkout in `vat-engine.int.test.ts`). I ran these in my own database on 2026-10-04: 283 unit, PGlite and render tests, 314 integration tests and the 4 e2e tests (a rebuilt app, real Chromium) passed. Still short of Full: (1) every consumer-visible text of the invoice (`src/lib/invoice-text.ts`, nb, sv, da, en) and the admin warnings are hand-written and unreviewed, and the content list (4.3 of the spec) rests on Art. 226 read through the UK legislation mirror (EUR-Lex would not load), Norway's bokforingsforskriften 5-1-1, Skatteverket and Denmark's guidance, with Germany from a secondary source and every other member state unread, so by docs/parity/WAVES.md step 4 the row is not Full until a person has read them (spec section 8); the national-currency VAT line, the buyer-address rule for downloads and the not-registered rendering (read for Denmark only) are the points most likely to change; (2) the order of the e2e is a fixture: `e2e/invoices.spec.ts` pays an order built by SQL through `complete_order_payment()` and proves the real Chromium PDF holds the number and total, the not-found for a foreign token, the print fallback and no cookie, but no spec presses Checkout (a test database has no Stripe); the checkout kinds scenarios in `checkout-kinds.int.test.ts` pay with a fake Stripe, and issue the invoice only after the store's test account is switched to live for one call; (3) never exercised: a PDF stored in Supabase Storage, Chromium on Vercel for the three new routes (`outputFileTracingIncludes`), `/api/cron/document-pdfs` is not scheduled anywhere, and nothing ran against production; (4) invoicing is off for stores that already have real orders until the owner turns it on, and no invoice is made for earlier orders (stated in the spec, section 7); (5) a venue-only booking's snapshot still stores a payment day and supply date equal to the confirmation day; the document no longer draws them, and unit 1c does not read them; (6) not built, by the spec: simplified invoices, exemption references for exempt lines, custom templates, structured e-invoices, other languages, and any country beyond NO, SE, DK, DE and the Directive.
criteria: A paid order gets an invoice in the store's own gap-free invoice series, issued once and immutable, with seller and buyer details, VAT per rate and the order's currency (database and integration tests, as `issue_work_invoice`).
The shopper can always download a legal invoice PDF from the order page, the order email links it and attaches the PDF when it exists, and staff can reprint it (render and integration tests).
A business order carries the buyer's company and VAT number and the reverse-charge note when it applies.
Copied history and hosts' orders never get an invoice from this store.

shopify.text: App. Shopify issues no credit note natively, and the free Order Printer app does not support credit notes, gift receipts or draft orders; invoicing apps from the App Store do.

gap: Built and held by tests (unit 1b, D159, in production): a deferred constraint trigger on refunds issues one credit note, in its own gap-free series, at commit for every refund that becomes `succeeded`, by any path (`refundOrder()`, order cancel, booking cancel, the AI tool, D153 returns, the new Stripe `refund.created`/`refund.updated` handler `applyStripeRefund()`, a refund made in Stripe's Dashboard, raw SQL), allocated by the largest-remainder method over the invoice's VAT rates (`creditAllocation()`), never above what the invoice has left per rate (a database trigger), with the VAT in the seller's currency summing exactly to the invoice's; a return's refund is one note with its working (`returns.refund_working`: goods at their rates, deduction, delivery, return shipping, adjustment), a return refunded outside Kaizen gets its note from the return, and the refund email links it and attaches the PDF when it exists. I ran these in my own database on 2026-10-04: the PGlite, unit and integration tests listed all passed. Still short of Full: (1) the credit note's wording, the treatment of a deduction and of return shipping (do they reduce the credited VAT) and the not-registered rendering are hand-written and unreviewed, and the legal basis is the same partly secondary reading as the invoice's, so by WAVES.md step 4 the row is not Full until a person has read them; (2) the Stripe webhook endpoint must be told to send `refund.created` and `refund.updated` in test and live (only the lead can check it in Stripe's Dashboard); until then a refund Stripe reports later, or a refund made in the Dashboard, is seen only by the job that asks Stripe about Kaizen's own pending refunds, and the handler was tested against a fake Stripe only; (3) the rule that a refund of a payment that is not on the invoice (a no-show fee) gets no credit note (`payment_on_invoice()`: made no later than the invoice and named by no `booking.no_show` event) is a heuristic that a future fee payment of another kind could slip past; (4) a refund Stripe reports as failed after it succeeded changes nothing and is only reported by the checkup, with no corrective document (stated in the spec, section 7); a staff retry of a refund the webhook already recorded is refused when nothing is left to refund; (5) no manual credit note, no credit for a cancelled order that was never refunded, no corrective invoice or void (wave 3); (6) the PDF, Storage, Chromium on Vercel and production are unproven as for the invoice row.
criteria: Every refund that succeeds on an order that has an invoice produces a credit note in the store's gap-free credit-note series, linked to the invoice, with the refunded amount and VAT per rate; refunds on host, copied, Stripe-test-mode or invoicing-off orders, and pending or failed refunds, produce none until they succeed (database and integration tests).
A return's refund (D153) produces one credit note with its working; the refund email links it and attaches the PDF when it exists, and the shopper can always download it from the order page.
A credit note is immutable and cannot exceed what the invoice left uncredited.

history.why: Unit 1b (D159 proposed) read in the working tree and run in a fresh database on 2026-10-04: invoices.test.ts and invoices-money-review.test.ts (every refund path P1 to P10, one note per refund, own series, over-invoice refused, no credit for a no-show fee), credit-allocation.test.ts, invoice-refunds.int.test.ts (refundOrder, the refund webhook, pending then succeeded, replays), invoice-returns.int.test.ts (a return's working, refunded outside) and checkout-kinds.int.test.ts (every kind, in euro, refunded in parts) all pass, so the gap that a shop order's refund produced no credit note is closed in the code. Held at partial because the wording is unreviewed legal text (WAVES.md step 4) and nothing runs in production yet.

shopify.text: App. Shopify's own gift receipts exist only for POS sales; online, gift messages and printed gift receipts come from App Store apps (Giftnote, Gift Ship, Wrapit and others); the free Order Printer app does not do gift receipts.

criteria: At checkout the shopper marks an order as a gift with a message of at most 300 characters (60 for each name); it is kept on the order and shown to staff (integration test).
The packing slip of a gift order shows the message and no prices. No email is ever sent to the gift's recipient, and the shipping notice to the buyer never carries the message.
The message passes through the same output cleaning as other shopper text and is never rendered as HTML.

history.why: Wave 3 run 2 (docs/wave-3-orders.md, D173 proposed; working tree not committed, migration not applied to production). Read gift.ts (`cleanShopperText()`, `cleanGift()`: no zod, refused not cut), cart.ts `setCartGift()`, the copy in `placeOrder()`, the frozen-gift trigger, the cart box, the order page's Gift card, `packingSlipData()` and the slip view, and `sendOrderConfirmation()`/`sendShipped()`; ran on a fresh database: gift.test.ts, gift-no-html.scan.test.ts, orders-ops.test.ts (PGlite: fields, limits, frozen, anonymised), gift.int.test.ts, checkout-kinds.int.test.ts (gift scenarios in krone and euro), packing-slip-views.test.ts, order-page-views.test.ts, order-export-ops.int.test.ts, and e2e/gift.spec.ts (4 passed) on a fresh production build of the final tree. The spec promised a test that `sendShipped()` never carries the message and that no email goes to anyone but the buyer; it did not exist, so `src/server/gift-shipping.int.test.ts` was added in this step (the confirmation repeats the message for the buyer, the shipping notice carries neither the message nor the recipient's name, every email of the order is to the order's own address) and passes. G2 and G1 are read as the spec's criteria changes say: no email to a recipient exists, and the lengths are 300 and 60. Caveat: the gift words are interface text hand-written in nb, sv, da and en and the buyer's text about a third party raises the GDPR questions of spec section 8 item 8; no test clicks the staff's order page or the slip route.
